content: Sydney Children’s Hospital is a pediatric hospital located in the Eastern Suburbs of Sydney, New South Wales, Australia. It is situated approximately 6 kilometers from the Sydney Central Business District in the suburb of Randwick. The hospital serves as a major teaching facility and is affiliated with the University of New South Wales. The origins of Sydney Children’s Hospital date back to 1852 with the establishment of the Society for Destitute Children. This organization opened the Asylum for Destitute Children on March 21, 1858, in Paddington. In 1870, following a fundraising appeal, the Catherine Hayes Hospital was opened. The hospital’s primary mission was to care for children suffering from illness, poverty, and famine. Over time, the children’s hospital became a dedicated wing of a larger general hospital. During the First World War in 1915, the hospital was repurposed by the New South Wales Government into a military hospital and later a repatriation hospital, renamed the Fourth Australian Repatriation Hospital. In 1927, a formal association was established between the Coast Hospital and the Fourth Australian Repatriation Hospital in Randwick. Following the opening of the Concord Repatriation General Hospital in 1953, the hospital was renamed the Prince of Wales Hospital, with the children’s hospital becoming known as the Prince of Wales Children’s Hospital. In 1964, the Prince of Wales Children’s Hospital was established as an independent institution under the leadership of Professor John Beveridge, who envisioned a hospital dedicated to the care of children. That same year, it became the teaching hospital for the University of New South Wales. A redevelopment project costing 5 million AUD significantly enhanced the hospital’s capabilities. On June 12, 1998, the Prince of Wales Children’s Hospital was officially renamed Sydney Children’s Hospital. The renaming ceremony was conducted by the then New South Wales Premier, Bob Carr, and Dr. Andrew Refshauge at 11:00 AM. In 2003, the hospital expanded its services by opening a community child health facility on the Randwick campus. This facility provides specialized care for children with developmental disabilities, mental health disorders, and other behavioral issues.
